neutral_facts.value: The accused appellant and the main accused were related to each other. There was a previous enmity between them over a land dispute. On the day of the incident, the accused appellant stopped the victim on his way and told him not to cultivate his land. A quarrel started between the victim and the accused appellant. The main accused intervened, whereupon the victim told him not to interfere and to go home as he was not involved in the dispute. The main accused took out a pistol from his pocket and pointed it at the victim. The victim told the main accused not to open fire, whereupon the accused appellant urged the main accused to kill the victim. The main accused then fired the pistol, causing injury to the victim with splinters. The prosecution alleged that the accused appellant instigated the main accused to kill the victim. However, the court found that the prosecution failed to establish a pre-arranged common intention between the accused appellant and the main accused to kill the victim. The court also noted discrepancies in the evidence of the victim and other witnesses, raising doubts about the truth and accuracy of their accounts. The court concluded that the accused appellant did not carry arms or open fire and that the main accused acted on his own initiative.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to establish a pre-arranged common intention between the accused appellant and the main accused to kill the complainant, and that the main accused acted on his own initiative without any instigation from the accused appellant.

quotes.text: The Prosecution miserably failed to establish any common, premeditated or prearranged intention jointly of the accused appellant and the main accused to kill the complainant, on the spot or otherwise.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that common intention is necessary for joint liability under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, and that pre-arranged intention must be established through proved facts and circumstances.

quotes.text: It is a settled principle of criminal law that only the person who actually commits the offence can be held guilty and sentenced in accordance with law.
Section 34 is only a rule of evidence which attracts the principle of joint criminal liability and does not create any distinct, substantive offence.
